text:
maya: quick follow-up from the egress-connector RFC — we need to lock down the compatibility story before we land the new control-plane split. main concerns: connector API changes, cert/handshake semantics, and a safe rollout path.

sam: thanks — can you summarise the compatibility matrix you have in mind? are we talking breaking HTTP paths, or just adding headers/flags?

maya: mostly additive headers + a small handshake change where connectors advertise their capability set. but the handshake will change wire semantics slightly (we add `capabilities` and `cp_routing_hint`). not planning to drop old fields immediately.

jon: +1 for additive, but we should version the handshake response. e.g. `Handshake-Proto: v1` / `v2` so older connectors keep working. that makes router logic easier: if v1 -> fallback routing, if v2 -> route via private endpoint.

rachel: can we do feature-flag gated behavior on the control plane so we can flip new routing for a subset of tenants? we should also capture metrics to detect mistaken fallthroughs.

maya: yes to both. plan sketch:
- handshake is backward compatible (connectors that don't send `capabilities` are treated as v1)
- control plane reads capability + tenant policy to decide routing
- rollout via FF: 0% -> 10% canary -> 50% -> 100%

sam: what about the cert lifecycle? with CP separation we might have two CA roots (cp-managed vs tenant-managed). connectors need to present an attestation to both. what's the minimal change to avoid requiring all customers to rotate keys?

maya: proposal A (minimal change): keep single client cert for connector, add opaque attestation token that control plane verifies. connector attaches token in handshake: `Attestation: <signed-jwt>`. CP rotates verification keys independently.

jon: Proposal B (more secure): connector mints ephemeral certs per session via CP-signed CSR. downside: needs PKI plumbing + latency.

dave: from infra viewpoint, A is way easier for rollout. B has better forward secrecy but is a bigger ops lift. also watch out for NAT hairpin implications when connector switches between cp-relay vs per-tenant endpoint — SNAT mappings might change and break existing flows.

rachel: we should add an integration test that simulates connector switching routes mid-flow and ensures requests either fail closed or gracefully fallback. also add a metric `connector_route_change_rate` and an alert threshold.

maya: agreed. I'll file the follow-up checklist. quick pseudo-handshake for doc (will put in RFC appendix):

```
Client -> Connector: CONNECT {token}
Connector -> CP: HANDSHAKE {connector_id, capabilities?, attestation?}
CP -> Connector: HANDSHAKE_RESP {proto_version, routing_hint, cp_ca_thumbprint}
Connector -> Client: PROXY_OK
```

sam: small nit — ensure we include `grace_period` in HANDSHAKE_RESP so connectors know how long v1 semantics are acceptable. saves a lot of flakiness during cutovers.

maya: good call. will add `grace_window_seconds`.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: feature-flag platform.egress_v2 created in prod. owners: @maya @dave.

jon: next steps from engineering: 1) add handshake version header, 2) gate CP routing behind FF, 3) end-to-end test harness, 4) canary plan doc.

rachel: ops: we'll prepare canary tenants and have SLO rollback playbook ready.

maya: thanks all — i'll update the RFC appendix and open the follow-up PRs. tagging @sam for API review. :thumbsup:

sam: got it — will review the API shapes today. :eyes:
